summary: Chi-chiang Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD from the University of Arizona by 1986, studying under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao and teacher Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from UCLA by 1993, having studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and held a teaching assistant post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Chie Ikeya is a historian and archaeologist who completed a PhD at Cornell University by 2006, where she studied under David K. Wyatt.

Chien Y. Hsu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Hsu studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura (through 2011) and James B. Apple (attested 2013), as well as traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013).

Chien-hsing Ho works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn, Nobuyoshi Yamabe, and Canshan Cheng, and became an Assistant Professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2016).

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1907–1910) and the University of Tokyo. He became the first professor at Keijo Imperial University in 1927 and also held a post at Yamaguchi University.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the University of British Columbia and a PhD from the University of Calgary, studying under Leslie S. Kawamura, Karin Preisendanz, Ashok Aklujkar, and others.
Chiko Corona is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura (attested 2010).
Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1970) and as a part-time lecturer (attested 1980).

Ching-mei Shyu specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed an MA at the University of Hawaii under Jan Nattier and a PhD at Cornell University by 2008 under Daniel Boucher, Jane-Marie Law, and Hubert Durt.
Chishō Namai (born 1947) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Koyasan University, where he served as a professor (attested 1996) and as president (attested 2008).

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) works in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Kyoto University (~1964–1968), he served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1979–1983) and as a professor at Tokoha University (attested 1989).

Chizuko Yoshimizu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Vienna, worked at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies, and became a professor at the University of Tsukuba.
Chlodwig H. Werba is an Indologist and linguist who served as a professor at the University of Vienna (attested 1997–2006, 2022) and taught Vitus Angermeier.
Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kunga Chöphel, Geshe Tsechok, and Zimwok Rinpoche, he was appointed the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Nalendra Monastery in 1928.

Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche (born 1951) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. Having studied under teachers including Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, he founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and trained under traditional teacher Daehaeng Kun Sunim (attested 2012).
Chris Clark specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Sydney by 2015 under Mark Allon and served there as an honorary associate (attested 2019).
